Done. I read `Servex/readme.md` and `Servex/doc/processes.md` (the `load_module` MCP tool wasn't grantable in this session, so I read the files directly — same content).

Note: this session is sandboxed to the worktree only, so the file landed at the worktree's mirror path rather than the literal monorepo path you gave:
`C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\process-monitor\public\framework\ai\2026-09-30\process-monitor\docs-check.md`

**Verdict:** the docs are usable — someone could operate the monitor, the orphan reaper, and worktree clean-up from them alone. Biggest gap: no documented way to force an immediate check cycle (everything is timer-only, 10s/10min), plus the `GET /api/processes` response shape is never shown as an example. Full list is in the file (6 gaps, ranked).

The task has landed. Summary:

**Built** the Processes section on the Live card (`/framework/ai2/live/`) in `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/process-graph`: a RAM/CPU graph with a shared hover crosshair, by-task rows with sparklines (top 5 open, rest folded), orphans, and the worktree count — all from Servex's new `GET /api/processes`. "Running now" agent rows also gained their real process (pid/MB or "no process"/"dormant, no process").

**Found and fixed two real bugs** along the way, both in my own `ai2.css`, caught by headless measurement rather than by eye: a closed `<details>` that wasn't actually collapsing (an author `display` rule beat the browser's own hide-when-closed behavior), and a reused grid class that squeezed the row's `<summary>` into an 88px column, word-wrapping its text. Both are written up in `ai2/doc/processes.md` so the next person touching this doesn't reintroduce them.

**Proved** it headless at 400/1200/1920, light and dark, with zero console/page errors on the touched page. Committed on `worktree/process-graph`; landed in the task log with a full report and screenshots at `/framework/ai/2026-09-30/process-monitor/graph/graph-report.md`. Reported to the parent mastermind (`task-mastermind-dormant-idle`), who owns the merge once the rest of the process-monitor task's pieces are ready.

The message delivered. Summary of this round:

Fixed all three issues the parent's shot review flagged, all inside my fence (`ai2.css`/`live.js`/`processes.js`), none requiring a framework-level change:

1. **The ~650px gap above Processes at 1920** — Processes was its own grid row placed after both columns, so it waited for the taller one (tasks + chat) to finish. Fixed by giving Running now and Processes one shared box (`.ai2-live-run-col`) that carries the grid area — Processes now starts the instant Running now's own list ends.
2. **Worktrees' ~100px indent** — it was reusing `.ai2-live-item`'s 4-column grid (built for a badge+name+line+✕ row), which pushed its text into column 3. Now a plain two-line box, flush left like Orphans.
3. **By-task/Orphans rows all different widths** — traced to `framework.css`'s global "control grammar," which gives every bare `<summary>` a button look including `width: fit-content`. `.ai2-proc-row`'s summary now explicitly opts out (the same way a couple of other modules on the site already do), so rows now stretch full width and the numbers/sparklines line up in a column.

Verified each fix numerically (gap: 650px → 16px; row width: matches parent width exactly now; indent: 110px → 6px) before trusting the screenshots. Re-shot 400/1200/1920 in light and dark, updated `graph-report.md` with before/after and `ai2/doc/processes.md` with the two new traps, committed as `c61efbb1` on `worktree/process-graph`, and reported back to the parent mastermind, who owns the merge from here.
